question: Nia had 51 handmade candles ready for a market. She made 30 more on Saturday and was given 36 by her friend Otto, who had made fewer candles than Nia. She then tripled her whole stock by working through a long weekend. A wholesaler added 65 candles for her to sell on their behalf. Shoppers bought 266 candles during the market. How many candles did Nia have left?

On Monday morning a depot had 235 pallets of bottled water. Later that morning a supplier delivered 77 more, and in the afternoon a returned order added 53. In the evening 69 pallets were sent out to a festival. Every pallet still in the depot carries 9 crates of bottles. The supervisor Nils counted more crates than his colleague Aina did on her own aisle. The depot logs its loading times in minutes even though the haulage contract is written in hours. How many crates were in the depot?

A community garden had 34 tools in its shed, a dozen of them long-handled, and bought 4 more. 11 tools were returned to the lender they had come from. A grant then paid for 49 new tools. 3 tools were broken during a work day, and 3 replacements arrived the next morning. Every tool in the shed needs 7 minutes of cleaning after use, and the garden adds those minutes up. The rota is written in minutes although the volunteers' agreement talks about hours. How many minutes of cleaning does one full round of the shed take?

On Monday morning a school hall had 69 chairs stacked at the back, and the caretaker brought in 72 more. Every chair carries 6 rubber feet, and the caretaker counted the feet before an inspection. Later that morning he found 5 spare feet in a drawer. The hall itself is 32 metres long. During the afternoon 511 worn feet were stripped off and thrown away. In the evening a delivery brought 5 replacement feet. How many rubber feet did the caretaker count at the end?

A library had 155 audio players to lend out. 96 of them were borrowed in the first week, and 57 more went out in the second. The library is open 6 days a week. 1 player came back broken and was scrapped. A donor named Elke then gave the library 22 players, which was more than her colleague Toma had ever donated. How many audio players did the library have available?

On Monday morning a warehouse held 210 sacks of rice, and a delivery added 10 more. At midday the stock was split evenly, and the manager kept half of the sacks at the main site while the rest went to a second store. During the afternoon 48 sacks were sold from the main site. Later that afternoon a returned order brought 63 sacks back to it. In the evening 68 sacks were driven from the main site to a food bank. How many sacks were left at the main site?

Amara had 168 packets of glass beads and tripled that stock at a craft fair. Her cousin Felix then gave her 48 more packets, although Felix owns fewer packets than Amara does. The fair itself lasted 4 days. Every packet holds 9 beads. Each bead is cut with 9 flat facets. How many facets were there on all of Amara's beads?

A bakery began with 40 kilograms of flour and divided it equally between its 2 ovens, setting the first oven's share aside. A supplier added 18 kilograms to that share. Every kilogram in it makes 5 rolls, and the bakery counted the rolls. A cancelled order returned 41 rolls, and a second bakery sent over 43. The rolls were then split equally between 2 shops, and the shop on Mill Street took one of those parts. The bakery records its proving times in minutes even though the recipe cards give them in hours. How many rolls went to the Mill Street shop?

A cinema had 201 rolls of ticket paper in its store and bought 58 more. A venue that closed sent over 23 rolls. A busy season used up 59 rolls, and a supplier then delivered 35. The chain tripled that whole stock when it took over a second cinema with an identical store. The chain measures its film lengths in minutes although the listings are printed in hours. A last delivery added 9 rolls. How many rolls of ticket paper did the chain hold?

On Saturday morning a bike shop that has traded for 25 years had 98 spare tyres in its stockroom. 8 tyres were fitted before lunch. In the early afternoon a delivery brought 60 more tyres. Later that afternoon the tyres were shared equally among the 3 branches, and the High Street branch took one of the shares. In the evening 12 tyres were sold from that branch. The shop records repair times in minutes although the price list quotes hours. How many tyres did the High Street branch have left?

On Monday morning a school kitchen had 18 crates of fruit and doubled that number with an emergency order. Later that morning a farm donated 47 crates. During the afternoon 29 crates were sent to a sister school, which left that school's cook Baptiste with fewer crates than the head cook Marie still had. In the evening Marie had every crate she kept repacked into 3 boxes. Each of those boxes was then filled with 9 pieces of fruit. How many pieces of fruit did Marie's kitchen hold?

A depot took in 168 bundles of newspapers and pulped 37 of them as unsold. Each remaining bundle holds 8 newspapers. Every newspaper carries 5 advertising inserts. The identical delivery is made to 7 towns. The manager Ivo counted more inserts than his colleague Dana did on her own round. The depot logs its delivery times in minutes even though the contract with the printers is written in hours. How many inserts were delivered in total?

A car park attendant issued 222 tickets at each of the 4 gates one morning. By the end of the day 762 of those tickets had been handed back at the exit. A coach party then took 58 tickets, and a late event accounted for 79 more. The attendant Yara kept a bigger tally than her colleague Emeka did at the side gate. The car park records stay lengths in minutes although its charges are advertised by the hour. How many tickets were still in circulation?

A gym had 69 lockers in the main changing room and installed 31 more. Every locker is issued with 6 wristbands over a season, and the gym counted those wristbands. A supplier sent 29 spare wristbands. Members lost 49 wristbands during the season. The gym records class lengths in minutes even though the timetable on the wall is set out in hours. How many wristbands did the gym have?

On Monday morning a farm shop had 20 trays of eggs and collected 27 more from the hen houses. Before lunch 33 trays were sold to a hotel. In the afternoon every tray still in the shop was emptied and the eggs were boxed 6 to a box. In the evening the shop learned that an identical delivery had to be prepared for each of 7 markets. How many boxes of eggs did the shop prepare in all?

A theatre company had 86 costumes in store and hired 53 more. A touring production then took 132 costumes away. The wardrobe department bought 75 costumes at an auction and inherited 76 from a company that closed. The rehearsal room is 18 metres long. A fire inspection condemned 108 costumes. Every costume that survived was hung with 6 accessories. How many accessories were hung?

Devon started the month with 128 minutes on his music-practice card. He used 119 minutes preparing for an audition, then his teacher added 29 minutes as a reward and his aunt bought him 62 more. He divided the minutes then on the card equally into 5 identical daily slots and kept just one slot on his own card, passing the rest to his sister. A rescan glitch cost him 2 minutes, and the studio credited him 46 minutes for a lesson it cancelled. The studio prints these credits in hours on its noticeboard, but Devon always counts his in minutes, and half of the practice rooms were closed for painting that week. How many minutes are on Devon's card now?

Ana's orchard had 209 apple trees, and she planted 5 more before the harvest. Every tree in the orchard filled 9 baskets. Each basket held exactly 8 apples. At the cider house every apple was cut into 2 pieces. Ana's neighbour Beto brought his own fruit and ended up with fewer pieces than Ana, so she tipped his 55 pear pieces and his 74 plum pieces into her pile as well. How many pieces are in Ana's pile now?

On Monday morning a nursery had 50 lavender cuttings, and a supplier delivered 54 more. By noon the head grower had divided every cutting he held into 7 rooted plugs. In the afternoon a customer returned 45 plugs. During the evening market 596 plugs were sold. Overnight the propagation bench turned each plug still on site into 5 new plugs. How many plugs does the nursery have now?

A hardware shop opened the day with 125 tins of white paint. It sold 67 tins to a decorating firm and 19 tins to walk-in customers. A cancelled order put 60 tins back on the shelf, and the afternoon delivery brought 43 more. The chain's warehouse then restocked the aisle so that the shop held 4 tins for every tin it had at that moment. Half of the aisle's shelving had just been repainted grey. How many tins of white paint does the shop hold now?

Early on Saturday morning a print shop loaded 193 sheets of card into the cutter, and each sheet was cut into 8 labels. Mid-morning a customer brought 65 labels of her own to add to the tray. At lunchtime the machine reprinted the whole tray, producing 3 labels for every label present. During the afternoon 4762 labels were shipped to a supermarket. In the early evening the shop ran a final pass that made 7 copies of every label left in the tray. Just before closing, 270 labels failed the quality check and were binned. How many labels remain in the tray?

Marisol had 72 minutes of pool time saved on her swim pass. She used 46 minutes at Tuesday's session, and her coach added 10 minutes for helping tidy the lane ropes. The centre then split what was left on her pass equally between the 4 members of her relay team, giving each member the same number of minutes. Marisol's own share was then granted to her again in each of the 6 weeks of the summer programme. The noticeboard lists pool time in hours even though passes are always issued in minutes, and half of the pool was roped off for lessons. How many minutes of pool time does Marisol get across the whole summer programme?

A community garden had 91 tomato plants at the start of June. A late frost killed 44 of them, and 20 more were dug up to make room for a new path. The gardeners then took cuttings until the plot held twice as many plants as it did once the path was finished. Each of those plants was later split into 9 separate pots for the summer plant sale. A neighbour donated 38 extra potted plants to the sale. How many potted plants does the sale have?

A youth club's badge box held 22 sheets of stickers, and each sheet carried 6 badges. The leader handed out 67 badges at the first meeting of the term. A sponsor then tripled the number of badges the club still had. The badges were sorted equally into 3 identical tins, and only one tin was taken to the summer camp. At camp every badge in that tin was swapped for 5 enamel pins. How many enamel pins came back from camp?

A school choir had 45 minutes of hall time booked, and the caretaker added 25 minutes more. The booking was split equally across the 5 weekdays, and only the Wednesday block stayed in the choir's name. A clash with the science club shortened that block by 10 minutes. The choir then held that same block in each of the 8 weeks of the autumn term, and the county trust paid for the identical programme to run in each of 7 different schools. The hall timetable is written in hours although bookings are made in minutes, and the choir has 31 members. How many minutes of hall time does the trust pay for altogether?
